stem: For the linear function \(f\), \(f(0) \ne 0\) and \(f(6) = 4\). In the \(xy\)-plane, the \(x\)-coordinate of the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) is 3 times the \(y\)-coordinate of the \(y\)-intercept. What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the \(x\)-intercept?
solution: Let the \(y\)-intercept be \((0, b)\), with \(b \ne 0\). Then the \(x\)-intercept is \((3b, 0)\), and the slope is \(\frac{0 - b}{3b - 0} = -\frac{1}{3}\), whatever \(b\) is.
verify:
x, b = symbols('x b', nonzero=True)
m = Rational(0 - 1, 3)  # slope (0 - b)/(3b)
assert simplify((0 - b)/(3*b) - m) == 0
f = m*x + b
bs = solve(Eq(f.subs(x, 6), 4), b)
assert bs == [6]
ans = solve(Eq(f.subs(b, 6), 0), x)[0]
assert ans == 18 == 3*bs[0]
assert len(spr_answers) == 1 and Rational(spr_answers[0]) == ans
